steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for low heat and lightly oil the grate.
Wrap each potato with a piece of bacon and secure with a toothpick. Sprinkle each wrapped potato with powdered ranch dressing mix.
Cook on the preheated grill, turning potatoes several times to allow bacon to cook on all sides. Potatoes are done when bacon is crispy, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon-Wrapped New Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Bite-sized new potatoes are wrapped in bacon and grilled until crispy. Serve this grilled appetizer with ranch dressing or BBQ sauce for dipping.
raw_recipe.name: Bacon-Wrapped New Potatoes

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for low heat and lightly oil the grate.
Wrap each potato with a piece of bacon and secure with a toothpick. Sprinkle each wrapped potato with powdered ranch dressing mix.
Cook on the preheated grill, turning potatoes several times to allow bacon to cook on all sides. Potatoes are done when bacon is crispy, 20 to 25 minutes.

review.reviewBody: These were pretty tasty and would make them again next time without the ranch dressing mix. It made them a little too salty. Next time I will roll in garlic olive oil and wrap in the bacon. Depending on the size of your potatoes you might need more bacon. I did par boil my potatoes - cooled and then wrapped them in bacon. They can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator. They are a bit fiddley to assemble - but easy and fast to grill. Keep your eye on them though so they don't go up in flames! *** Yes, these can be done in the oven. Might make for a tasty appetizer.
These were DELISH! Everyone loved them. We used turkey bacon and wrapped the entire slice of bacon a round it. A little piece of heaven.

These were fantastic! I par-boiled the new potatoes and then instead of using ranch mix (which I find too salty) I coated them with olive oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper and then wrapped them with thick bacon (Wright's) and baked on a broiler pan in the oven for 20 minutes or so at 400 degrees. We dipped them in sour cream and they were to-die-for. Thanks!

I was a little short on time, so I boiled my new potatoes for about 8 minutes, then sliced them in half and put them in cold water so I could stand to handle them! I drained them and coated them with olive oil, then rolled them in ranch season mix (recipe on this site). I warped 1/2 slice of bacon around each, using toothpicks to hold the bacon on. Placed the taters on a broiler pan, sprinkled grated sharp cheddar cheese on them and baked them for about 20 minutes. I took these to a pool party - everyone loved them!

I made these for a Labor Day party and changed up a few things, but frankly this is a winning combo that would be hard to mess up.
I made about 75 for the party (they were gone within 1 hour) so I ended up baking them in my oven. Just too many for the grill.
I used baby golden potatoes that I poked with a fork after washing. and placed in a large zip lock back with vandalia onion dressing, fresh ground pepper, a splash of evoo and let sit overnight in the fridge.
I wrapped the potatoes with thick cut bacon (tucked the ends on the underside) from GFS (my fav) in the morning and again placed back in the fridge until I was ready to bake. This helped the bacon to set around the potatoe nicely without using toothpicks. I baked them at 400 for about 45 minutes and they were perfect. I served with a side bowl of 'Sweet Baby Rays BBQ Sauce"
Next time I might sprinkle with some finely shredded cheddar cheese at the very end of baking, or maybe try these with a bit of brown sugar sprinked on top when rolling up, and just before placing back in the fridge.
As I said, this is just one of those recipes that whatever you do, it will be great tasting, and make you look like a wonder in the kitchen!

I melted butter in garlic in a sauce pan. Put in some fingerling potatoes & stirred. I did not cook the potatoes. Let them cool in the butter then wrapped them in bacon. Grilled slow on the grill & they were delicious! The garlic & butter gave them the flavor I was looking for. The bacon was crisp. I dipped them in light sour cream. 
I will make them again for sure!

Wonderful recipe! Made these as an appetizer with a few changes. Infused olive oil with rosemary, garlic powder, a small amount of the ranch dressing and pepper. Par boiled the potatoes and poured the olive oil mixture over the potatoes. After wrapping potatoes in bacon poured remaining olive oil mixture over all and let sit in refrigerator for a few houses. Baked for 45 minutes. Definitely will be making these again.

I love this recipe but I tweaked it just a little. Although the Ranch dressing on the potatoes sounds great, I skipped this part all together. I did not dress the potatoes but I did sauté them in a little butter and oil then once they were browned a little I sprinkled them with some black pepper and onion powder and drained them on papper towel. I then wrapped them in the bacon an threw them in the oven for about 25 minutes until the bacon was cooked, browned and a little crispy. The potatoes were nice and soft and fluffy inside; their skins were a little crispy because I had already browned them first before I wrapped them in bacon. They were gone in seconds after being put out on the table! Very yummy!!!

Easy and delicious! I did par boil, then bake the potatoes instead of putting them on the grill. After baking I broil them for a few minutes to crisp the bacon. I used thinly sliced bacon, which made wrapping easy. The thin bacon also crisped well. I used fingerling yukon golds. My personal favorite. The sweetness of the potato really worked with the ranch. I noticed quite a few people changed up the spices. I wouldn't. I think this is a wonderful dish, spiced perfectly! The family loved it! Thank you so much for sharing!

I made a simple change with the Ranch mix which added more Ranch flavor to the potatoes themselves rather than mainly flavoring the bacon. I poked the skins of freshly washed red potatoes really well, sprinkled the Ranch mix to taste directly on the still damp skins so the flavor would soak directly in to the potatoes and then wrapped with the bacon. Thank you for a fun and tasty recipe!

We loved these. My potatoes were a little larger than bite sized, so after par-cooking them (I steamed them) and wrapping them in par-cooked bacon, we tossed them on the grill to crisp them up. This was a huge hit with everyone at my table. We skipped the ranch mix on the potatoes and served them instead with a blue-cheese-ranch dip and they were fantastic. I'm pretty sure this will be asked for again and again by my family. These would also make a great appetizer for any party or gathering and could easily be cooked in the oven if the grill is not an option.
Very tasty!

Love these!! Family favorite. We use small red potatoes or butter potatoes. We also prefer coconut oil to the olive oil. I use a blend of Italian Seasonings as well. Use Creamy Italian as a dipping sauce. Delicious!!
Made them and enjoyed . Will make again

Easy and painless!
No wonder we made it as part of a Mother’s Day dinner everyone enjoyed. 
Kids dipped in ketchup, while adults added to their entree!
Awesome. Only used half the dressing. They do burn easily though so watch carefully.
made it as a main dish with fresh steamed vegetables and a glass of Coke. Yummmm
Not made it yet, as I do not have a grill. how would I make it on say, the hob/oven? (btw my boyfriend would love to have these but we live far apart atm, and he is saving for a house.)
Delicious! I didn't use the ranch packet just sprinkled a little seasoning salt, garlic and onion powder.
Delicious! Made in oven 400 for about 35 minutes. I partly boiled potatoes first.
